Maintain a connected ground condition to activate the frontage.
Keep the ground element compressed to preserve public openness.

Open the split enough to read as an occupiable court/entry seam rather than two nearly-colliding prisms.
Preserve a clear ground datum so the street edge can become active and legible.
Strengthen the base so the building reads as anchored to the access edge rather than hovering as separated fragments.
Keep the ground articulation low enough to form a public threshold instead of a bulky pedestal.
Reduce the upper visual aggression so the mass reads as calm residential/commercial hierarchy rather than a sculptural collision.

rationale: The candidate is legible as a split-wedge mass in all four views, so it is not a one-view trick, but it reads more like two colliding prismatic chunks than one continuous neighborhood-living figure. The blue access edge is not answered by a convincing public threshold: the ground condition remains mostly sealed, and the visible void is too small and semantically weak to count as an active street edge. The silhouette has some stepped/cut character, but the steps do not clearly bear terrace, ramp, or daylight meaning; they feel like clipped geometry. Program fit is therefore partial at best: neighborhood living can tolerate a compact bar or split mass, but here the dominant gesture does not yet establish the required active edge, public void, and calm hierarchical upper mass. The counterfactual 8 House suggests a transferable move: preserve the bar/split-wing datum, but carve a continuous, programmatic section void tied to access and terrace sequence rather than leaving the mass as a generic split block.
